Here's the family lineage:
- **Barack Obama II** (the 44th President of the United States)
  - Father: **Barack Obama Sr.** (born Baraka Hussein Obama in 1934, died 1982)

Barack Obama Sr. was a Kenyan economist who was educated at the University of Hawaii and Harvard University. **Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

**Stanley Armour Dunham** (March 23, 1918–February 8, 1992) was an American furniture salesman and the maternal grandfather of Barack Obama, a former President of the United States. He and his wife Madelyn Payne Dunham raised Obama from the age of 10 in Honolulu, Hawaii.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-freespirit-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-2)

## Early life and education
[edit]
Stanley Armour Dunham was born in Wichita, Kansas, the younger of two sons to Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Sr. and Ruth Lucille Armour. His father's ancestors settled in Kempton, Indiana, in the 1840s, before relocating to Kansas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-3) His parents were married on October 3, 1915, at a home on South Saint Francis St. in Wichita, and opened _The Travelers' Cafe_ on William Street situated between the old firehouse and the old Wichita City Hotel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5)
On November 25, 1926, at age 8, Dunham discovered his mother's body after she had committed suicide. Subsequently, Dunham's father placed him and his older brother Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Jr. in the care of their maternal grandparents in El Dorado, Kansas.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5) A rebellious teenager, Dunham allegedly punched his high school principal and spent some time drifting, hopping rail cars to Chicago, then California, and back again.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-6) He married Madelyn Lee Payne on May 5, 1940, the night of her senior prom.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Tribune1-7)

## Early life and education
Dunham enlisted as a private in the U.S. Army on January 18, 1942, at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, and served in the European Theatre of World War II with the 1830th Ordnance Supply and Maintenance Company, Aviation. During D-Day, this unit helped to support the Ninth Air Force. Dunham and his brother were deployed to France six weeks after D-Day. Before the Invasion of Normandy, the brothers once met accidentally as Stanley Dunham went in search of rations at a hotel in London, where his brother Ralph Dunham happened to be staying.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Benac-8) Madelyn Dunham gave birth to their daughter Stanley Ann Dunham, who was later known as Ann, at St. Francis Hospital in Wichita on November 29, 1942. During the war, Madelyn Dunham worked on a Boeing B-29 assembly line in Wichita.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-10)

## Early life and education
After two years of military service in Europe (1943–1945), Dunham was discharged from the U.S. Army on August 30, 1945. After the war, the family moved to Berkeley, California, so he could pursue study at the University of California, Berkeley and then eventually back to El Dorado, Kansas, where Dunham managed a furniture store. In 1955, after the Dunhams moved to Seattle, Washington, Dunham worked as a salesman for the Standard-Grunbaum Furniture Company, and his daughter Ann attended middle school. The family lived in an apartment in the Wedgwood Estates in the Wedgwood, Seattle neighborhood. In 1956 they moved to the Shorewood Apartments on Mercer Island, a Seattle suburb. Ann attended high school there, and they stayed until she graduated in 1960. In 1957, Dunham started working for the Doces Majestic Furniture Company.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-13)
The family then moved to Honolulu, Hawaii, where Dunham found a better furniture store opportunity. Madelyn Dunham started working at the Bank of Hawaii in 1960, and was promoted as one of the bank's first female vice presidents in 1970.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-death-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-tutu-15)

## Early life and education
In Barack Obama's memoir, _Dreams From My Father_, he wrote, "One of my earliest memories is of sitting on my grandfather's shoulders as the astronauts from one of the Apollo missions arrived at Hickam Air Force Base after a successful splashdown". At 10 years old, Barack Obama moved in with the Dunhams in Honolulu to attend school in the U.S. while his mother and stepfather Lolo Soetoro were living in Jakarta, Indonesia. His mother later came back to Hawaii to pursue graduate studies, but when she returned to Indonesia in 1977 for her master's fieldwork, Obama stayed in the United States with his grandparents. Obama wrote in his memoir, _Dreams From My Father_, "I'd arrived at an unspoken pact with my grandparents: I could live with them and they'd leave me alone so long as I kept my trouble out of sight".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Scott-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-17)
Dunham died in Honolulu, Hawaii, on February 8, 1992, and is interred in the Punchbowl National Cemetery.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Scott-16)
Dunham is a direct descendant of Jonathan Singletary Dunham, a prominent early American settler who left the Plymouth Colony to build the first gristmill in New Jersey.
The most recent native White European ancestor was Falmouth Kearney, a farmer who emigrated from Moneygall, County Offaly, Ireland, during the Great Irish Famine and settled in Jefferson Township, Tipton County, Indiana, United States. Kearney's youngest daughter, Mary Ann (Kearney) Dunham, was Stanley Dunham's paternal grandmother.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-18)

## Early life and education
In addition to his grandson Barack Obama, Stanley Dunham's distant relatives include six U.S. presidents: James Madison, Harry Truman, Lyndon Johnson, Jimmy Carter, George H. W. Bush and George W. Bush.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-22) Dunham and Wild Bill Hickok are sixth cousins, four times removed, through Jacob Dunham.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-23)

Hussein Onyango Obama September 9, 2007 BY SCOTT FORNEK Political Editor He was "a prominent farmer, an elder of the tribe, a medicine man with healing powers." He was born about 1895 in Kendu, Kenya. [3] [4] His parents were Obama and Nyaoke. [4] He left Kendu and moved to Alego. [4] Onyango had three wives. His first wife was Helima. [5] Helima could not bear children. [5] His second wife was Akumu. [6] Onyango and Akuma had three children: Sarah [6] Barack [6] Auma [7] His third wife was Sarah. Onyango and Sarah had four children: Omar [8][9] Zeituni [8][9] Sayid [9] Yusuf [9] He was such a strict disciplinarian that his grandchildren called him "the Terror." That's how Barack Obama describes his paternal grandfather, Hussein Onyango Obama, in his best-selling memoir Dreams From My Father. " 'Wow, that guy was mean!'" Obama quotes his half-brother, Abongo (Roy) Obama, as saying. " 'He would make you sit at the table for dinner, and served the food on china, like an Englishman. If you said one wrong thing, or used the wrong fork -- pow! He would hit you with his stick. Sometimes when he hit you, you wouldn't even know why until the next day.'" Grandfather Obama was an herbalist who knew how to use plants to heal the sick or wounded -- not " 'a shaman -- what the white man calls a witch doctor,' " Obama's step-grandmother Sarah Obama is quoted as saying. Hussein Onyango Obama worked for the white oppressors during the period of colonial rule in Kenya, first supervising rode crews and later working in a white man's home, after a two-week walk to Nairobi. " 'Later he would tell us the adventures he had during this journey,' " Sarah Obama is quoted as saying. " 'Many times he chased away leopards with his panga. Once he was chased into a tree by an angry buffalo and had to sleep in the tree for two days.

## Hussein Onyango Obama
Once he found a drum lying in the middle of the forest path and when he opened it, a snake appeared and slid between his feet into the bush.' " Obama's grandfather also served as cook for a British officer during World War II. His father was Opiyo and mother was Nyaoke. After hearing his step-grandmother's account, Obama writes that he was shattered, wondering whether his dead grandfather was an "Uncle Tom. Collaborator. House n-----." His step-grandmother tells Obama that her husband respected the white man's power, technology and self improvement, but he would never tolerate abuse and had even once beaten a white employer who tried to cane him. " 'If the white man he worked for was abusive, he would tell the man to go to hell and leave to find other work,' " she said. He didn't smoke or drink, but he did like to dance. " 'His only pleasure was going to the dance halls in Nairobi once a month, for he liked to dance,' " Obama's step grandmother says in the book. " 'But he also was not such a good dancer -- he was rough, and would bump into people and step on their feet.' "

He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.
texts.2: In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. **Stanley Armour Dunham** (March 23, 1918–February 8, 1992) was an American furniture salesman and the maternal grandfather of Barack Obama, a former President of the United States. He and his wife Madelyn Payne Dunham raised Obama from the age of 10 in Honolulu, Hawaii.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-freespirit-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-2)
texts.1:
## Early life and education
[edit]
Stanley Armour Dunham was born in Wichita, Kansas, the younger of two sons to Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Sr. and Ruth Lucille Armour. His father's ancestors settled in Kempton, Indiana, in the 1840s, before relocating to Kansas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-3) His parents were married on October 3, 1915, at a home on South Saint Francis St. in Wichita, and opened _The Travelers' Cafe_ on William Street situated between the old firehouse and the old Wichita City Hotel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5)
On November 25, 1926, at age 8, Dunham discovered his mother's body after she had committed suicide. Subsequently, Dunham's father placed him and his older brother Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Jr. in the care of their maternal grandparents in El Dorado, Kansas.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5) A rebellious teenager, Dunham allegedly punched his high school principal and spent some time drifting, hopping rail cars to Chicago, then California, and back again.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-6) He married Madelyn Lee Payne on May 5, 1940, the night of her senior prom.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Tribune1-7)
texts.2:
## Early life and education
Dunham enlisted as a private in the U.S. Army on January 18, 1942, at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, and served in the European Theatre of World War II with the 1830th Ordnance Supply and Maintenance Company, Aviation. During D-Day, this unit helped to support the Ninth Air Force. Dunham and his brother were deployed to France six weeks after D-Day. Before the Invasion of Normandy, the brothers once met accidentally as Stanley Dunham went in search of rations at a hotel in London, where his brother Ralph Dunham happened to be staying.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Benac-8) Madelyn Dunham gave birth to their daughter Stanley Ann Dunham, who was later known as Ann, at St. Francis Hospital in Wichita on November 29, 1942. During the war, Madelyn Dunham worked on a Boeing B-29 assembly line in Wichita.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-10)
texts.3:
## Early life and education
After two years of military service in Europe (1943–1945), Dunham was discharged from the U.S. Army on August 30, 1945. After the war, the family moved to Berkeley, California, so he could pursue study at the University of California, Berkeley and then eventually back to El Dorado, Kansas, where Dunham managed a furniture store. In 1955, after the Dunhams moved to Seattle, Washington, Dunham worked as a salesman for the Standard-Grunbaum Furniture Company, and his daughter Ann attended middle school. The family lived in an apartment in the Wedgwood Estates in the Wedgwood, Seattle neighborhood. In 1956 they moved to the Shorewood Apartments on Mercer Island, a Seattle suburb. Ann attended high school there, and they stayed until she graduated in 1960. In 1957, Dunham started working for the Doces Majestic Furniture Company.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-13)
The family then moved to Honolulu, Hawaii, where Dunham found a better furniture store opportunity. Madelyn Dunham started working at the Bank of Hawaii in 1960, and was promoted as one of the bank's first female vice presidents in 1970.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-death-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-tutu-15)

## Early life and education
In Barack Obama's memoir, _Dreams From My Father_, he wrote, "One of my earliest memories is of sitting on my grandfather's shoulders as the astronauts from one of the Apollo missions arrived at Hickam Air Force Base after a successful splashdown". At 10 years old, Barack Obama moved in with the Dunhams in Honolulu to attend school in the U.S. while his mother and stepfather Lolo Soetoro were living in Jakarta, Indonesia. His mother later came back to Hawaii to pursue graduate studies, but when she returned to Indonesia in 1977 for her master's fieldwork, Obama stayed in the United States with his grandparents. Obama wrote in his memoir, _Dreams From My Father_, "I'd arrived at an unspoken pact with my grandparents: I could live with them and they'd leave me alone so long as I kept my trouble out of sight".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Scott-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-17)
Dunham died in Honolulu, Hawaii, on February 8, 1992, and is interred in the Punchbowl National Cemetery.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Scott-16)
Dunham is a direct descendant of Jonathan Singletary Dunham, a prominent early American settler who left the Plymouth Colony to build the first gristmill in New Jersey.
The most recent native White European ancestor was Falmouth Kearney, a farmer who emigrated from Moneygall, County Offaly, Ireland, during the Great Irish Famine and settled in Jefferson Township, Tipton County, Indiana, United States. Kearney's youngest daughter, Mary Ann (Kearney) Dunham, was Stanley Dunham's paternal grandmother.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-18)

**Stanley Armour Dunham** (March 23, 1918–February 8, 1992) was an American furniture salesman and the maternal grandfather of Barack Obama, a former President of the United States. He and his wife Madelyn Payne Dunham raised Obama from the age of 10 in Honolulu, Hawaii.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-freespirit-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-2)

## Early life and education
[edit]
Stanley Armour Dunham was born in Wichita, Kansas, the younger of two sons to Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Sr. and Ruth Lucille Armour. His father's ancestors settled in Kempton, Indiana, in the 1840s, before relocating to Kansas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-3) His parents were married on October 3, 1915, at a home on South Saint Francis St. in Wichita, and opened _The Travelers' Cafe_ on William Street situated between the old firehouse and the old Wichita City Hotel.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5)
On November 25, 1926, at age 8, Dunham discovered his mother's body after she had committed suicide. Subsequently, Dunham's father placed him and his older brother Ralph Waldo Emerson Dunham, Jr. in the care of their maternal grandparents in El Dorado, Kansas.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Fornek-5) A rebellious teenager, Dunham allegedly punched his high school principal and spent some time drifting, hopping rail cars to Chicago, then California, and back again.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-6) He married Madelyn Lee Payne on May 5, 1940, the night of her senior prom.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Tribune1-7)

## Early life and education
Dunham enlisted as a private in the U.S. Army on January 18, 1942, at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas, and served in the European Theatre of World War II with the 1830th Ordnance Supply and Maintenance Company, Aviation. During D-Day, this unit helped to support the Ninth Air Force. Dunham and his brother were deployed to France six weeks after D-Day. Before the Invasion of Normandy, the brothers once met accidentally as Stanley Dunham went in search of rations at a hotel in London, where his brother Ralph Dunham happened to be staying.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-Benac-8) Madelyn Dunham gave birth to their daughter Stanley Ann Dunham, who was later known as Ann, at St. Francis Hospital in Wichita on November 29, 1942. During the war, Madelyn Dunham worked on a Boeing B-29 assembly line in Wichita.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-10)

## Early life and education
After two years of military service in Europe (1943–1945), Dunham was discharged from the U.S. Army on August 30, 1945. After the war, the family moved to Berkeley, California, so he could pursue study at the University of California, Berkeley and then eventually back to El Dorado, Kansas, where Dunham managed a furniture store. In 1955, after the Dunhams moved to Seattle, Washington, Dunham worked as a salesman for the Standard-Grunbaum Furniture Company, and his daughter Ann attended middle school. The family lived in an apartment in the Wedgwood Estates in the Wedgwood, Seattle neighborhood. In 1956 they moved to the Shorewood Apartments on Mercer Island, a Seattle suburb. Ann attended high school there, and they stayed until she graduated in 1960. In 1957, Dunham started working for the Doces Majestic Furniture Company.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham#cite_note-13)
The family then moved to Honolulu, Hawaii, where Dunham found a better furniture store opportunity.
